mainTopic: Can a גר תושב cancel an עבודה זרה, and how is a גר תושב defined and treated?
overview: The גמרא first brings a ברייתא supporting an earlier rule: a גר and a גוי may divide property that includes idol items only if they inherited it, not if they were partners. Then the sages ask whether a גר תושב, who has given up idol worship, can cancel an idol. רב נחמן says no, because only someone who worships idols can cancel one. The גמרא challenges him with a ברייתא saying a גוי can cancel an idol 'whether he worships it or not.' It answers that this means a גוי who serves a different idol. A second challenge comes from a ברייתא that defines a גר תושב, sets out rules for his wine, and says that in all other matters he is like a גוי. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that this line is about giving up rights in a shared courtyard on שבת, not about cancelling idols, and a ברייתא about apostate Jews and courtyard rights backs him up. The amud ends as a new story begins about a gift רב יהודה sent.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the inheritance-versus-partnership rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the earlier rule: the permission to divide property that includes idol items applies only to inheritance, not to partnership.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: When is this said? When they inherited. But if they were partners, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with the rule it just discussed. The permission applies when the property was inherited, but not when the two were partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule allowed a גר and a גוי to split their father's estate even though it includes idol items. The ברייתא limits this to inheritance. If they were business partners, which they chose to be, the split is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
In what case is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
They inherited
They became partners

steps.whatToRemember: The permission to divide shared property that includes idol items works only for an inheritance, not for a partnership.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
In what case is this said?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier rule that a גר and a גוי may split their father's property, even with idol items in it.

phrases.english: Where they inherited;
but if they were partners, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule discussed just before this section begins.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier rule that dividing shared property with idol items is allowed only for inheritance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same thing: inheritance is permitted and partnership is forbidden.

steps.title: Can a non-Jew who gave up idol worship cancel an idol?
steps.stepSummary: The sages ask whether a גר תושב can perform ביטול on an עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat again and a question was asked of them: Can a גר תושב cancel an idol? Maybe only someone who worships idols can cancel one, and someone who does not worship cannot. Or maybe anyone who belongs to the group of non-Jews can cancel, and a גר תושב belongs to that group?
steps.whatsHappening: The sages open a new question: can a גר תושב, a non-Jew who keeps the seven Noahide laws and does not worship idols, cancel an idol's forbidden status? The גמרא lays out two possible ways to think about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says the power to cancel belongs to people who actually worship idols, so a גר תושב cannot. Side two says it belongs to all non-Jews as a group, and a גר תושב is still a non-Jew. So the real question is whether the power depends on what the person does or on what group he belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who accepted the seven Noahide laws, including no idol worship
Cancels, meaning removes the forbidden status of an idol
Worships (Aramaic)
Or perhaps (brings the second side of a question)
One of its kind, part of the same group

steps.whyThisMatters: This question sets up the main argument of the section: does the power to cancel an idol depend on actually worshipping or simply on being a non-Jew?

phrases.english: They sat again and a question was raised before them:
phrases.notes: "They" are the same group of sages from earlier in the גמרא: רב נחמן, עולא, אבימי בר פפי and רב חייא בר אמי.

phrases.english: A ger toshav, what is the law
about his canceling an idol?
Is it that one who worships can cancel,
and one who does not worship cannot cancel,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֹּל דְּבַר מִינֵּיהּ מְבַטֵּיל,
phrases.english: or perhaps anyone who is of its kind can cancel,
phrases.notes: "Of its kind" means anyone from the group of non-Jews who generally worship idols.

phrases.english: and this one is of its kind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion among the same group of sages.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גר תושב, who does not worship idols, has the power to cancel an עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only one who worships can cancel
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that only someone who worships idols can cancel one, so a גר תושב cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: It makes sense that one who worships can cancel, and one who does not worship cannot cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by choosing the first side. A person who does not worship idols, like a גר תושב, cannot cancel an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן ties the power of ביטול to actually being an idol worshipper. Since a גר תושב gave up idol worship, he loses that power, even though he is still a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:
It stands to reason
that one who worships can cancel,
and one who does not worship cannot cancel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2 by choosing its first side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only someone who worships idols can cancel them, so a גר תושב cannot.

steps.title: A ברייתא says even a non-worshipper can cancel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא that says a גוי can cancel an idol whether or not he worships it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: A Jew who found an idol in the market may tell a גוי to cancel it, as long as it has not yet come into his hands. Once it has come into his hands, he may not tell a גוי to cancel it. This is because the sages said: a גוי can cancel his own idol and his friend's idol, whether he worships it or does not worship it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב נחמן's answer. The ברייתא ends by saying a גוי can cancel an idol even if he does not worship it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said only a worshipper can cancel. The ברייתא's last words, "whether he worships it or does not worship it," seem to say the opposite: a non-worshipper can cancel too. If so, a גר תושב should also be able to cancel, so the ברייתא seems to contradict רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Marketplace
It came into his hand, into his possession
Whether he worships it or does not worship it

steps.confusionAlert: The story about the Jew finding an idol in the market is not the challenge. The challenge comes from the last line: a גוי can cancel even an idol he does not worship.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A Jew who found an idol in the marketplace,
as long as it has not come into his possession,
he may tell a gentile, and the gentile cancels it;
once it has come into his possession,
he may not tell a gentile to cancel it;
because the sages said:
A gentile can cancel an idol,
his own or his fellow gentile's,
whether he worships it or does not worship it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that only someone who worships idols can cancel them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a גוי can cancel an idol even if he does not worship it. That suggests worshipping is not needed, so a גר תושב should be able to cancel too.

steps.title: Reading 'does not worship it' as a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that 'does not worship it' in the ברייתא must mean a גר תושב. If so, a גר תושב can cancel an idol, against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'worships it' mean, and what does 'does not worship it' mean? If both mean a גוי, that is the same as the earlier line, 'his own idol or his friend's.' So 'worships it' must mean a גוי, and 'does not worship it' must mean a גר תושב. We learn that a גר תושב can also cancel an idol!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out exactly how the ברייתא from the last step proves רב נחמן wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said a גוי can cancel his own idol or another's. If 'does not worship it' also meant a גוי, the line would just repeat itself. To avoid repeating, the גמרא reads it as a גר תושב, someone who serves no idols at all, and that goes directly against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; both phrases
That is the same thing (so it would be repeating)
Learn from it; we can conclude
Cancels the idol status of an object

phrases.english: What is meant by "worships it,"
and what is meant by "does not worship it"?
If you say both this and that mean a gentile,
that is the same as "his own or his fellow's"!
phrases.notes: This goes back to an earlier line in the same ברייתא: a גוי can cancel his own idol or another גוי's idol.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't "worships it" a gentile,
and what is "does not worship it"? A ger toshav,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נָמֵי מְבַטֵּל!
phrases.english: so learn from it that a ger toshav can also cancel an idol!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 4 contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that only someone who worships idols can cancel one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading both phrases as a גוי makes the ברייתא repeat itself, so 'does not worship it' must mean a גר תושב, who can therefore cancel.

steps.title: Both phrases mean a גוי: same idol versus different idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both phrases refer to a גוי. The first line covers two גוים who serve the same idol, and the later line covers two גוים who serve different idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, both phrases mean a גוי. As for your point that this repeats 'his own or his friend's': the first line is where both serve פעור, or both serve מרקוליס. The later line is where one serves פעור and the other serves מרקוליס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן by showing the ברייתא does not repeat itself even if both phrases are about a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His own or his friend's' teaches that a גוי can cancel an idol of the same kind he serves. 'Does not worship it' adds that he can cancel even an idol of a different kind that he does not serve. Since he is still an idol worshipper, רב נחמן's rule stands, and a גר תושב still cannot cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; in truth (used to hold on to the original reading)
The first clause
The later clause
Name of a known idol
Name of a known idol (Mercury)

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי can cancel even an idol he does not personally serve, because he is an idol worshipper. This leaves רב נחמן's rule in place.

phrases.english: No, really I will tell you:
both this and that mean a gentile,
and as for what you said, that it is the same as "his own or his fellow's":
the first clause is where this one and that one both serve Peor,
or this one and that one both serve Mercury;
the later clause is where this one serves Peor and that one serves Mercury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's reading of the ברייתא and defends רב נחמן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא so its two clauses teach different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If both phrases meant a גוי, the ברייתא would repeat itself, so one must mean a גר תושב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both mean a גוי. One clause covers the same idol and the other covers a different idol, so nothing repeats and רב נחמן stands.

steps.title: New challenge: who counts as a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two views on who is a גר תושב. רבי מאיר says it is anyone who accepts not to serve idols. חכמים say it is anyone who accepts the seven Noahide מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Who is a גר תושב? Anyone who accepted, in front of three חברים, not to serve idols. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: anyone who accepted the seven מצוות that the children of נח accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב נחמן by quoting a ברייתא about who counts as a גר תושב. This is setup: the actual point of the challenge comes in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have definitions. רבי מאיר defines a גר תושב by giving up idol worship alone. חכמים require the full seven Noahide מצוות. In step 13 the גמרא uses a later line of this ברייתא against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew living among Jews who accepted certain basic commitments
People known for careful observance of מצוות
The seven מצוות given to all humanity

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not yet say anything about cancelling idols. Don't look for the challenge here; the גמרא draws it out in step 13, after quoting the rest of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Who is a ger toshav?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵרִים
phrases.english: Anyone who accepted upon himself, in front of three ḥaverim,
not to worship idols,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
anyone who accepted upon himself the seven מצוות
that the descendants of Noah accepted upon themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא opens a second challenge built on the definition of a גר תושב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling in step 3 that a גר תושב cannot cancel an idol (the attack is drawn out in step 13).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא will go on to say a גר תושב is like a גוי in all other matters (step 12), which the גמרא reads in step 13 as letting him cancel an idol, against רב נחמן.

steps.title: A third view: a גר תושב keeps everything except נבילות
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say the people described by רבי מאיר and חכמים are not a גר תושב at all. A גר תושב is someone who accepts every מצוה in the Torah except the ban on eating נבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: those people are not considered a גר תושב. So who is a גר תושב? A גר who eats non-kosher carcasses, but who has accepted on himself to keep all the מצוות in the Torah except the ban on carcasses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 7 keeps going and adds a third opinion, from אחרים, about who counts as a גר תושב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר needed only a promise not to serve idols, and חכמים needed the seven Noahide מצוות‎. אחרים set a much higher bar: he must accept the whole Torah except one prohibition, eating נבילות. So we now have three definitions, each stricter than the one before.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a תנא quoted by this title
Have not entered the category of
Animals that died without a kosher שחיטה
A גר who still eats non-kosher carcasses

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with a full גר צדק. This person keeps almost everything, but because he has not accepted the ban on נבילות, he is still only a גר תושב.

phrases.english: Others say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ לֹא בָּאוּ לִכְלַל גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב,
phrases.english: These have not entered the category of a ger toshav,
Rather, who is a ger toshav?
This is a convert who eats unslaughtered carcasses,
who has accepted upon himself to observe
all of the מצוות stated in the Torah
except for the prohibition of carcasses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵלּוּ לֹא בָּאוּ לִכְלַל גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a third definition of גר תושב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אחרים, a גר תושב accepts all מצוות except the ban on נבילות.

steps.title: How a גר תושב's wine is treated
steps.stepSummary: Wine may be left briefly alone with a גר תושב, but it may not be deposited with him for a long time, even in a mostly Jewish city. Leaving it briefly is allowed even in a mostly non-Jewish city. His oil is like his wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may leave wine alone with him for a short time. But one may not leave wine in his keeping for a long time, even in a city that is mostly Jewish. But one may leave wine alone with him briefly even in a city that is mostly non-Jewish. His oil is like his wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives practical rules about a גר תושב and wine. Whichever definition we follow, these rules apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a גר תושב does not worship idols, we do not worry that he will pour the wine as an offering, so a short stay alone is fine. A long deposit is different, because he might swap it for a גוי's wine. That worry exists even in a mostly Jewish city.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave something alone with someone for a short time
Deposit something with someone for a long time
In a city that is mostly Jewish
His oil

steps.confusionAlert: מייחדין (a short time alone) and מפקידין (a long deposit) are two different situations. That is why one is allowed and the other is not.

phrases.english: One may leave him alone with wine,
but one may not deposit wine with him,
and even in a town that has a Jewish majority,
but one may leave him alone with wine
even in a town with a majority of gentiles.
His oil is like his wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְיַיחֲדִין אֶצְלוֹ יַיִן, וְאֵין מַפְקִידִין אֶצְלוֹ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining a גר תושב to the rules about his wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A short stay alone with wine is allowed. A long deposit of wine with him is not.

steps.title: Oil cannot be like wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording 'his oil is like his wine.' Oil never becomes יין נסך, so it makes no sense to compare it to wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His oil is like his wine'? Can you really think that? Does oil ever become wine poured to an idol?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the ברייתא to attack one phrase that does not make sense as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern with wine is that it might be poured as an offering to an idol and become יין נסך. Oil is never used that way. So saying his oil follows the rules of his wine cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)
Wine poured as an offering to an idol
Does it become?

phrases.english: His oil is like his wine? Can this enter your mind?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן מִי קָא הָוֵי יֵין נֶסֶךְ?
phrases.english: Does oil become libation wine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last line of the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'שמנו כיינו' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wine rules exist because of יין נסך, and oil can never become יין נסך, so the comparison makes no sense.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: his wine is like his oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the phrase around. It should read 'his wine is like his oil.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: his wine is like his oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by correcting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the oil is the model and the wine follows it. His wine gets the same status as his oil: one may benefit from it, but not drink it. So the wine is not treated as real יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: His wine is like his oil

steps.whatToRemember: A גר תושב's wine is not real יין נסך. Like his oil, one may benefit from it but may not drink it.

phrases.english: Rather: his wine is like his oil.
phrases.notes: This means one may benefit from his wine, like his oil, but may not drink it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 10 by reversing the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as printed makes oil follow the rules of wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading makes wine follow oil: benefit is allowed, drinking is not.

steps.title: Other matters, and רבן שמעון's view on his wine
steps.stepSummary: In all other matters a גר תושב is like a גוי. רבן שמעון says his wine is יין נסך. Others report that רבן שמעון says it may even be drunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in every other matter he is like a non-Jew. רבן שמעון says: his wine is יין נסך. And some say he says: it may even be drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes. It gives the general rule for a גר תושב and then quotes רבן שמעון, whose view is reported in two opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's middle position is that one may benefit from his wine but not drink it. In the first version, רבן שמעון is stricter: the wine is treated like real יין נסך. In the second version, he is more lenient: even drinking is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And for all other matters
Permitted to drink

steps.whatToRemember: There are three positions on a גר תושב's wine: forbidden like יין נסך, allowed for benefit only, or allowed even to drink.
steps.confusionAlert: The two reports of רבן שמעון's view are not two separate rulings. They are two opposite reports of what he held.

phrases.english: And with regard to all other matters
he is like a gentile.
Rabban Shimon says:
His wine is libation wine,
and some say: it is permitted for drinking.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁאָר כׇּל דָּבָר הֲרֵי הוּא כְּגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the wording in steps 10-11, goes back to finish the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In other matters a גר תושב is like a גוי. רבן שמעון's view on his wine is reported as either fully forbidden or fully permitted.

steps.title: Trying to prove a גר תושב can nullify an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the ברייתא's line that a גר תושב is like a גוי in all other matters, and suggests this means he can nullify עבודה זרה like a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: 'In all his other matters he is like a גוי.' What halacha does this come to teach? Isn't it that he can nullify an idol, just like a גוי can?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 12 and tries to use one line from it as a proof. The claim is that a גר תושב can nullify עבודה זרה like a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a גר תושב is like a גוי 'in all other matters' but does not say which matters. The גמרא suggests the main example is ביטול עבודה זרה. A גוי can nullify an idol, so a גר תושב could too.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches. Used to pull one useful line out of a source.
For what halacha? Which practical law does this teach?
Nullifies an idol, so that it loses its forbidden status.
A non-Jew who lives among Jews and has accepted certain מצוות.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְלִשְׁאָר כׇּל דְּבָרָיו הֲרֵי הוּא כְּגוֹי.
phrases.english: And in all his other matters, he is like a גוי.
For what halacha is this said?
Is it not that he can nullify an idol, like a גוי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a line from the ברייתא quoted in step 12 as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a גר תושב can nullify עבודה זרה like a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line 'ולשאר כל דבריו הרי הוא כגוי'.

steps.title: The line is about courtyard rights, not idols
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof: 'like a גוי' refers to giving and giving up rights in a courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: No. It is about giving rights and giving up rights in a shared area.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק turns down the proof from step 13. He says the line about being 'like a גוי' is about the laws of a shared courtyard on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא never names the 'other matters,' the line could point to a different law. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it teaches that a גר תושב, like a גוי, cannot simply give up his share of a courtyard. So nothing is proven about nullifying an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: A domain, here a person's share or rights in a shared courtyard.
To give one's rights in the courtyard to others.
To give up one's rights in the courtyard, so others may carry there on שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a person's house or property in general. It is about the שבת rules of a shared courtyard, where one neighbor's share can stop everyone from carrying.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: No,
it is about giving rights in a domain and giving up rights in a domain.
phrases.notes: He means the line 'he is like a גוי' teaches that a גר תושב cannot do this the way a Jew can.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of the ברייתא. It does not decide whether a גר תושב can nullify an idol.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'like a גוי' means nullifying idols, but it can refer to the courtyard laws of רשות.
steps.whyThisMatters: After this answer, the ברייתא no longer proves anything about a גר תושב nullifying עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא on which apostate Jews can give up courtyard rights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an apostate Jew who keeps שבת in public can give up his courtyard rights, but one who does not cannot, because only a Jew can give or give up such rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: An apostate Jew who keeps his שבת in the marketplace can give up his rights. One who does not keep his שבת in the marketplace cannot give up his rights. This is because the Sages said: A Jew can give rights and give up rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב נחמן בר יצחק and show where this courtyard law comes from. It explains which kind of apostate Jew counts as a Jew for this purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a Jew can simply give up his share of a courtyard. An apostate who still keeps שבת in public is treated as a Jew for this. One who breaks שבת in public is treated like a גוי. This fits the claim that a גר תושב is 'like a גוי' in this matter.

keyTerms.meaning: And as it is taught in a ברייתא. Brings a source that agrees.
An apostate Jew, one who has left Jewish practice.
Keeps his שבת in the marketplace, meaning in public.

phrases.english: And as it is taught in a ברייתא:
An apostate Jew who keeps his Shabbat in the marketplace,
phrases.notes: 'In the marketplace' means in public, where people can see him.

phrases.english: can give up his rights in the domain.
One who does not keep his Shabbat in the marketplace
cannot give up his rights in the domain,
because the Sages said:
A Jew gives rights in a domain and gives up rights in a domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting the courtyard law that רב נחמן בר יצחק referred to.
steps.raayaObject: That 'giving and giving up רשות' is a known law where some people are treated like a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an apostate Jew and courtyard rights.

steps.title: With a גוי the share must be rented, and how a Jew gives up his share
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: with a גוי the courtyard share must be rented. A Jew gives up his share by simply saying 'my share is acquired by you' or 'my share is given up to you,' and no formal act is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a גוי, it does not work until it is rented. How does a Jew do it? He says to the other: 'My rights are acquired by you,' or 'My rights are given up to you.' The other person acquires them, and no formal act of acquiring is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its rule. It contrasts a גוי, whose share must be rented, with a Jew, who can give up his share with words alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows exactly why being 'like a גוי' matters here. A Jew's spoken words are enough, and the other Jew does not have to do a formal act to take possession. For a גוי, words are not enough, and his share must be rented.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he rents. The courtyard share must be rented.
How so? Introduces an explanation of how something is done.
Acquired by you.
To take possession through a formal act of acquiring.

steps.whatToRemember: A גר תושב is 'like a גוי' for courtyard rights. A Jew, even an apostate who keeps שבת in public, gives up his share with words alone. With a גוי, the share must be rented.

phrases.english: But with a gentile, it does not work until it is rented.
How so? He says to him:
'My rights in the domain are acquired by you,'
or 'My rights in the domain are given up to you,'
he has acquired them, and he does not need to take possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the ברייתא from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a גוי, the courtyard share must be rented. A Jew gives up his share by words alone, with no formal act of acquisition.

steps.title: A new story begins: רב יהודה sends a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story: רב יהודה sent a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה sent him a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story here. This line only sets the scene, and the story continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only know that רב יהודה sent a gift to someone. Who received it, and why the story matters, comes in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent to him.
A gift or present.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda sent him a gift

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after the courtyard discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This sets up a story that continues in the next lines.
